All 6 facts confirmed on their Wikipedia pages via WebFetch: Messinian salinity crisis (start 5.96 +/- 0.02 Ma, 'precursor of the Strait of Gibraltar closed about 5.96 Ma'; ended with Gibraltar reopening 5.33 Ma; net evaporative loss ~3,300 km3/yr; 3.7 million km3 in the basin; no consensus on full drying, brine lakes remained -> script's 'most ... gone' and 'salty lakes' fit; Nile canyon cut ~2,500 m below sea level), Strait of Gibraltar infobox min width 14.2 km (body text says 14.3 km); evaporation exceeding river inflow confirmed; Zanclean flood: Garcia-Castellanos max ~100 million m3/s, 90% filled in months to two years, a modelled estimate attributed 'By one estimate'. Topic verify items met. Description ends with the channel disclaimer. Notes: at 5.96 Ma the connection was the strait's precursor / Betic-Rifian corridors (fine as a simplified map); 'slammed shut' is dramatic for a tectonic, repeated closure - style only.
